subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I notice the mane blades appear as dark, spiky black thorns sticking out of the neck instead of the intended gradient look, even though the root and tip colors should produce a lighter shaded blade — something in the extrusion or coloring logic is making them render too dark.

Beyond that, the brow and cheek blocks look like black flaps cluttering the face, the head shape is oddly blocky with a flat hanging jaw, and the mouth gap reads too wide from the side. The body is a bit tubular but otherwise fine, the banner placement works even though it's partly obscured in front view, and the tail with its dark tip looks okay.

I'm deciding to remove the brow boxes entirely rather than recolor them, relying instead on the painted cream brow spots, and to shrink the oversized black nose ball significantly.

For the eyes, I'm enlarging the orange decals and shifting them slightly forward, checking that they clear both the skull's curved surface and the muzzle frustum so they don't end up hidden or clipped.

For the mane, I want to lighten the ring blade colors from a darker gray to a lighter cream tone, and widen the ridge for a softer look, since the lighting was making them render too dark and stiff.

I'm also considering adding a Frostwolf-style accent — maybe a leather collar with a glowing blue-stone pendant at the neck, built as a closed catmull ring swept around the neck joint at roughly radius 0.19 to sit comfortably over the neck geometry.

I'm reconsidering the pendant placement since the chest/belly orientation doesn't line up well with a forward-tilted neck, so I'll skip the pendant and instead keep the collar simple, adding small gold studs placed at each item along the ring using the item's inherited position data.

Checking other details now: paws, lighting, floor placement, jaw thickness, and ear tips all look fine as-is, so I'll leave them alone and skip adding extra decorative elements like floating ice shards or banner glow to keep the edits focused. Moving on to writing the actual edit for removing the brow boxes, making sure the search text matches exactly.

For edit two, replacing the brow geometry with a small fur-colored wedge shaped as a blob using the existing helper function, positioned near the brow area with the head fur color. For the eye decal edit, I need to be careful since the same position coordinates appear in multiple places with different formatting, so I have to match the exact whitespace and line structure to avoid replacing the wrong instance.

Adjusting the eye decal to be larger and positioned slightly more forward, which will create a small mismatch with the painted eye socket underneath -- updating the socket coordinate variable to match keeps things aligned. Then there's the nose scale edit, mane color updates, ridge color and width widening, and finally adding a collar ring positioned along the neck's tangent frame after the ridge calls, sized to match the neck's radius.
